Subject: Post-call synopsis & pilot charter (next steps)

Hi Samir / Alyssa —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same alignment before we kick off the pilot. Please reply with any changes or confirmations.

What we heard (pain & goal):
- Pain: production NLU throughput is inconsistent under bursty traffic; caching and batching at the model layer are brittle and driving high per-token cost.
- Goal: reduce median latency for inference from ~420ms to <200ms for single-turn queries, and bring per-call cost down by ~30% for the search assistant workload.

Success metrics for the PoC (agreed):
1) Median latency <200ms for 95% of calls at target QPS (25 requests/s)
2) End-to-end cost per 1k queries reduced by >=30% vs current baseline
3) Prompt-eval pass rate >= 92% on the provided 500-sample prompt suite

Scope & timeline (proposed):
- Duration: 6 weeks (kickoff week + 5 sprint weeks)
- Week 0 (this week): access + service account + small sample data ingest
- Week 1: baseline run and initial prompt/eval sweep
- Week 2–4: optimization (batching, prefix cache, quantization profile testing)
- Week 5: acceptance run, final eval, handoff notes

Owners & RACI (tentative):
- QuantumGrid: Alyssa Chen (Product Owner), Raj Kumar (Infra) — provide sample dataset & approve access
- Redwood: Tessa Morgan (AE, engagement lead), Karthik Iyer (SE, onboarding & optimizations)

Access checklist (what we need from your side):
- Create a service account for redwood-onboard@quantumgrid (or share a temporary API key)
- Upload a 500-row sample of representative prompts + expected outputs to the Drive folder linked below
- Allow outbound traffic to Redwood IPs (we'll send the range) or provide a sandbox VPC peering window

Attachments: QuantumGrid_PoC_Charter_v1.pdf (charter & success gates), access-setup-instructions.md (step-by-step).

Immediate asks: confirm owners (Alyssa / Raj), and confirm you can provide the sample data by Friday 09/03. If SOC2 evidence review is needed, please loop in your security contact and we’ll share the SOC2/pen test summary.

Thanks — looking forward to kicking this off.

—
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Thanks — I’ll drive the technical onboarding and the prompt-eval runs. A few tactical notes from the SE side:

Pre-run checklist (I’ll add these to Drive):
- Sample set: please include 500 rows with columns {prompt_id, input_text, expected_label, context_tags} and a short README.
- Data sensitivity: if any rows contain PII flag them; we can scope a masked-run alternatively.
- Service account: either a short-lived API key or the service account with role \"redwood-pilot-ingest\" will work.
- Env: we’ll spin a 3-node trial env with the same model family you plan to use (will confirm model id once we see sample length distribution).

Prompt-eval matrix (example metrics we’ll publish weekly):
- Accuracy / pass-rate against expected_label (binary pass/fail rules)
- Median & 95th latency at target QPS
- Cost per 1k queries (tokens computed from sample)
- Failure modes (truncation, hallucination, timeout) with representative examples

Deliverables from Redwood this week:
- Baseline report + baseline eval (09/08)
- Optimization plan (09/15)
- Interim evals weekly, final acceptance report 10/05

If you can drop the sample set link into the Drive folder and confirm Raj as networking contact, I’ll queue the peering diagnostic and calendar invites.
